old: Long before symbols and equations, people worked out sums by moving small stones around.
The Latin word behind this one, calculō, literally meant reckoning with pebbles.
It's a cousin of "calculus" — both trace back to calx, the Latin word for limestone.
clues: This verb for a kind of careful mental work traces back to a Latin word for a little pebble, built from the word for limestone.
To work out an amount or answer using math, more precise than estimating and more involved than simply counting. Its Latin ancestor meant reckoning by means of pebbles.
You might do this to figure out the tip at dinner. It shares its pebble root with calculus, which became the name of a whole branch of mathematics.
